prompt_text: My AC needs repair in Houston. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you a short list of reputable HVAC companies that serve Houston and explain why they’re worth calling — plus what to ask them and how to choose between estimates. Before I refine the list to companies closest to you, can you tell me your ZIP code, whether this is residential or commercial, and whether it’s an emergency (no cool air right now)?

Meanwhile, here are 4 companies you can call now and why:

1. John Moore Services (Houston)
- Why call: Locally based, long-standing Houston company that handles emergency repairs, maintenance, and full system replacements. Large local presence means fast same-day service in many areas.
- What they’re good for: Residential emergency repairs, seasonal tune-ups, and replacements backed by local reputation.

2. ARS/Rescue Rooter (Houston)
- Why call: Nationally known with big local footprint; offers 24/7 emergency HVAC service, standardized diagnostic processes, and financing options. Useful if you need an urgent after-hours call.
- What they’re good for: Quick emergency response, standard repairs, and major replacement jobs where financing or flexible scheduling helps.

3. One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (Houston franchises)
- Why call: Franchise network with on-time guarantees and transparent pricing policies. Technicians typically carry industry certifications, and the company emphasizes punctual service.
- What they’re good for: Fast service windows, clear arrival times, routine repairs and diagnostics.

4. ABC Home & Commercial Services (Houston)
- Why call: Offers comprehensive residential and commercial services, preventive maintenance plans, and extended warranties. Good if you want ongoing maintenance or a service contract after the repair.
- What they’re good for: Planned maintenance, service contracts, and warranty-backed replacements.

How to choose which to call (quick vetting checklist)
- Confirm license and insurance: Ask for the contractor license number and proof of liability insurance.
- Ask about technician certification: Look for NATE certification or manufacturer training.
- Get a written estimate: Should list parts, labor, diagnostic fee (if any), and warranty terms.
- Emergency/after-hours fees: Ask about extra charges for nights/weekends.
- Warranty on parts and labor: Ask what’s covered and for how long.
- Ask for references or recent reviews: Check Google, Yelp, Angi, and BBB for recent feedback in your neighborhood.
- Get 2–3 estimates for major repairs/replacements before committing.

What to ask on the phone (if you call now)
- “Can you give me a service window and on-call/after-hours policy?”
- “Do your techs carry NATE or manufacturer certifications for my brand?”
- “What is your diagnostic fee and is it waived if I proceed with repair?”
- “Do you offer financing, and what warranties do you provide on parts and labor?”

If you share your ZIP code and the symptoms (no cool air, short cycling, strange noises, leaks, tripped breaker), I’ll pull 2–3 more highly-rated local companies very near you and recommend which to call first depending on urgency.
